pages.text: Proton-antiproton annihilation turns mass entirely into pions: about half the energy in charged pions (p ≈ 0.35 GeV/c), a third in gamma rays, the rest in neutrinos. A magnetic nozzle can catch the charged pions if their gyroradius p/(0.3B) fits the 3 m chamber; the gammas must be stopped by shielding.
$(thing)Set$(): Nozzle field, Antimatter feed, Gamma shield.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Annihilation-point jitter: capture varies by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Gamma flux through the shield is melting the structure; Interlock: magnetic nozzle not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the magnetic nozzle quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Generator output follows the captured power.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Annihilation power: P = 2ṁc²$(br)Pion gyroradius: r_g = p/(0.3B)$(br)Capture fraction: f = 1 − r_g/R$(br)Electric power: P_e = ½P·f$(br)Gamma power: P_γ = ⅓P$(br)Escaping gammas: P_γ·e^(−x/20 cm)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)
